stem: A client without cancer receives a germline genetic-test result showing a pathogenic BRCA1 variant. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: The result means the client has an increased risk for several cancers, but it does not predict with certainty whether or when cancer will develop; individualized risk-management counseling and discussion with blood relatives are appropriate.
options.B: The result means the client already has occult breast or ovarian cancer even if current diagnostic evaluation is negative.
options.C: The result guarantees that the client will develop cancer, so routine screening is no longer useful.
options.D: The result has no implications for blood relatives because inherited BRCA variants affect only the person who was tested.

rationale: NCI states that an inherited harmful or pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant increases the risk of several cancers but does not determine with certainty whether or when cancer will occur; some carriers never develop cancer. People who inherit a harmful variant may consider enhanced screening and other individualized risk-reduction strategies after counseling. Because a germline variant is inherited, test results may also be relevant to blood relatives, who can use that information to better understand their own potential cancer risk. A pathogenic variant indicates susceptibility, not a current cancer diagnosis.
educational_objective: Interpret a germline pathogenic BRCA result as inherited cancer susceptibility rather than a cancer diagnosis or guarantee, and recognize its implications for individualized prevention/screening and family risk communication.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: BRCA Gene Changes: Cancer Risk and Genetic Testing Fact Sheet
source_locator: What do BRCA1 and BRCA2 genetic test results mean? — Positive result; Who should consider genetic counseling and testing?; How can a person with an inherited harmful change manage cancer risk?
source_claim_supported: NCI states that a positive germline BRCA result indicates a harmful/pathogenic variant and increased cancer risk but cannot predict whether or when cancer will develop; results may inform enhanced screening/risk reduction and may have implications for blood relatives.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — interpretation of inherited BRCA cancer susceptibility and preventive planning
correction_summary: Rebuilt the original broad 'positive mutation' item using current NCI terminology for pathogenic/harmful germline variants. Clarified that the result indicates susceptibility rather than certainty or current cancer, retained family implications without overstating inheritance outcomes for any specific relative, and remapped the construct from Reduction of Risk Potential to Health Promotion and Maintenance because it centers on hereditary risk assessment, screening, prevention, and counseling.
audit_findings: Original item was directionally correct but used imprecise 'positive mutation' language and framed risk interpretation as a generic oncology-monitoring concept.
Fresh NCI review explicitly states that pathogenic BRCA variants increase cancer risk but do not determine whether or when cancer will occur.
NCI supports enhanced screening/risk-reduction discussion and sharing inherited-test information with blood relatives who may have related risk.
The final item does not imply that a pathogenic variant is itself a cancer diagnosis or that any relative necessarily carries the variant.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct explanation with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, deterministic genetic claim, or unresolved source conflict.
